title: Application security and authorization — Module Quiz
description: Course assessment: Ensure each user sees only their own expenses.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Whether an identity may perform an operation on a resource

questions.explanation: Authorization is about permissions, including object ownership.

questions.prompt: Is a valid login sufficient to read any expense id?

options.text: Only if the id is numeric

questions.explanation: Each resource still needs an authorization check.

questions.prompt: Does a signed JWT necessarily conceal its payload?
questions.explanation: Signing protects integrity, not confidentiality of the encoded payload.

questions.prompt: Is CORS a substitute for server-side authorization?
questions.explanation: Non-browser clients and same-origin requests still need access controls.

questions.prompt: Which requests need deliberate CSRF consideration?

options.text: State-changing requests using ambient browser credentials such as cookies

questions.explanation: Browsers may attach cookies to requests initiated by another site.

questions.prompt: Where should the owner of a newly created expense come from?

options.text: An unchecked owner field in the body

questions.explanation: The caller must not assign arbitrary ownership or privileges.
The application receives an established user identity. alice matches the expense owner and may read it. bob is authenticated but is not authorized for this expense.
